{"description":"A Decision whose idea is sound and whose moment is wrong can be recorded as set aside in a field the coherence loop reads, so it leaves the "what needs me" list without being rejected, superseded, or quietly left to look live.

MEASURED 2026-09-11: 690 Decisions against a status vocabulary of proposed | accepted | superseded | rejected. Ten say DEFERRED in prose and twenty say WITHDRAWN, against four carrying `rejected` in the field — and one node is literally named "DEFERRED, SHAPE ONLY —" while its status reads `proposed`. People are recording the state; they are recording it where nothing can read it. (The thirty is a substring count over decision text — a floor on the pressure, not a census.)

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: a `proposed` Decision carrying an approver edge is DEBT — loop_status reports it as owed and what_next ranks it. A deferred idea is not debt, and today it sits in the same bucket as a live question somebody is waiting on. Every deferred idea makes the list slightly less true, and a list that degrades is how a person learns to stop reading it.

SCOPED TO `deferred`, NOT TO `withdrawn`, DELIBERATELY: the test for a candidate state is not whether the distinction is real but WHAT WOULD READ IT. For deferral there is an answer — loop_status and what_next both change behaviour. For withdrawn there may not be one.

SEQUENCED BEHIND THE VOCABULARY GUARD: adding an enum value moves nothing the version guard reads, so shipping this first would demonstrate that exact bug on reflow2's own graph.","name":"A decision set aside is recorded in a field a computation can read, so the loop stops counting it as work somebody owes","provenance":"authored","status":"planned","tier":"operational"}
